title: Recipe Struct
story: Your friend keeps losing their grandmother's recipes. You decide to digitize them. Each recipe has ingredients (name, amount, unit) and serving info. Structs are a perfect fit for this structured data.
why: Not everything needs methods — sometimes structs are just for organizing and carrying data.
analogy: A recipe card has sections (title, servings, ingredients). A struct is the digital version of that card — each field is a line on the card.
try_it: Create 3 different recipes (pancakes, cookies, smoothie). Write a function that takes a list of recipes and returns the one with the most servings. No collections needed — just compare them with if/else.
tips: Data-only structs are perfectly valid — not every type needs methods
Name your structs after real-world nouns: `Ingredient`, `Recipe`, `Invoice`
Use `Float64` for measurements that need decimals (grams, cups, liters)
common_mistakes: Creating every struct as mutable — use `let` for values that don't change
Forgetting to copy all fields when creating a modified version of a struct
